resources.name: units
resources.title: Units and their definitions
resources.description: Every unit with a fixed factor: its value in the base unit of its category, whether the definition is exact, and the official source. The temperature scales and fuel-economy units are defined by formulas, given in units.json.

sources.title: NIST SP 811, NIST Handbook 44, BIPM SI Brochure, NIST binary prefixes, UK Weights and Measures Act 1985

resources.name: conversions
resources.title: Converter factors
resources.description: One row per converter page: multiply the 'from' value by the factor to get the 'to' value. Temperature pairs use the formulas in units.json.

sources.title: Derived with exact arithmetic from units.csv

resources.name: conversion-values
resources.title: Common conversion values
resources.description: The values that have their own page on the site (for example 37 °C in °F), converted with the factors above.

resources.name: awg
resources.title: AWG wire geometry
resources.description: Diameter and cross-section of American Wire Gauge sizes 4/0 to 40, from the defining formula d = 0.005 in × 92^((36 − n)/39) (ASTM B258). Ampacity is not included.

sources.title: Computed from the AWG formula (ASTM B258)

resources.name: npt-threads
resources.title: NPT pipe thread basic dimensions
resources.description: American Standard taper pipe threads (NPT): threads per inch, outside diameter, pitch diameters E0 and E1, hand-tight engagement L1 and effective thread length L2, in inches.

sources.title: NBS Handbook H28 (1957), Part II, Table VII.2 (US government publication, public domain); checked 7 November 2026

resources.name: water-density
resources.title: Density of pure water, 0–40 °C
resources.description: Density of air-free pure water at 101.325 kPa and the weight of one US gallon, from the CIPM-recommended formula.

sources.title: CIPM formula, Tanaka et al., Metrologia 38 (2001) 301–309, as published by NIST

resources.name: boiling-point-altitude
resources.title: Boiling point of water by altitude
resources.description: Standard-atmosphere pressure and the boiling point of pure water from sea level to 8,849 m.

sources.title: IAPWS R7-97(2012) Region 4 equation; U.S. Standard Atmosphere, 1976

resources.name: wind-chill
resources.title: Wind chill table
resources.description: Wind chill temperature in °F for air temperatures from 40 °F to −45 °F and wind speeds from 5 to 60 mph.

sources.title: National Weather Service wind chill formula (2001)

resources.name: tasks
resources.title: Task paths
resources.description: Common engineering jobs as ordered steps across the site's pages.

resources.name: verification
resources.title: Verification records
resources.description: What was checked against which official source, when, for which pages.
